sections.h2: How big is Boston and what is it bordered by?
sections.html:
Boston is the capital and largest city in Massachusetts, and it lies in Suffolk County. Its total area is about 89.6 square miles, but only 48.3 square miles of that is land. The other 41.3 square miles is water.

The city is bordered by several communities that matter when you compare sale prices and property tax bills:

  • Winthrop and the Boston Harbor Islands to the east
  • Revere, Chelsea and Everett to the northeast
  • Somerville and Cambridge to the north
  • Watertown to the northwest
  • Newton and Brookline to the west
  • Dedham, with small portions of Needham and Canton, to the southwest
  • Milton and Quincy to the southeast

The Charles River separates Allston-Brighton, Fenway-Kenmore and Back Bay from Cambridge and Watertown. The Neponset River forms the line between southern Boston and Quincy and Milton. The highest point in the city is Bellevue Hill at 330 feet.

sections.h2: What are the neighborhoods of Boston?
sections.html:
The city's Office of Neighborhood Services recognizes 23 neighborhoods, which is why Boston is often called a city of neighborhoods. Your neighborhood affects how a house sells more than the city name does.

AreaNeighborhoods
Downtown coreDowntown or Financial District, Beacon Hill, West End, North End, Chinatown, Bay Village
Central and waterfrontBack Bay, South End, Seaport District, South Boston, East Boston, Charlestown
West and southwestAllston, Brighton, Fenway-Kenmore, Mission Hill, Jamaica Plain, Roslindale, West Roxbury, Hyde Park
SouthRoxbury, Dorchester, Mattapan

Boston also has 53 ZIP codes, so check the ZIP and the neighborhood on your assessment record instead of assuming they match.

sections.h2: How did Boston's land and housing take shape?
sections.html:
Boston was settled in 1625, named in 1630 and became a city in 1822. More than two thirds of the modern land area of inner Boston did not exist when the city was founded. It was created by filling tidal areas, using earth from leveling the three original hills and gravel brought by train from Needham to fill Back Bay.

That history shows up in the housing. Back Bay has single family homes along with wooden and brick multi-family row houses. The South End Historic District is the largest surviving contiguous Victorian era neighborhood in the country. Downtown and South Boston have low rise masonry buildings in Federal and Greek Revival styles beside modern towers.

The Central Artery/Tunnel Project, known as the Big Dig, ran from 1991 to 2007 and replaced the elevated highway through downtown with tunnels, new green spaces and open areas. The South End is a designated historic district, so if your house is in an area like it, ask the city whether review rules apply to exterior work.

sections.h2: How dense is Boston, and why does it matter to sellers?
sections.html:
Boston is the most densely populated state capital in the country, and the third most densely populated large US city of more than half a million residents. Its density is about 13,977 people per square mile of land.

The daytime population is larger than the resident count. Around 1.2 million people may be inside city limits during work hours, and as many as 2 million during special events, because suburban residents commute in. For a seller, that means on-street parking, building access and noise are real selling points or objections, and buyers will ask about them when they walk the house.

sections.h2: What employers drive the Boston economy?
sections.html:
Health care and education dominate Boston's employer list. The city ranks among the top 30 most economically powerful in the world according to Wikipedia, and the Greater Boston metro area had a GDP of about $645 billion in 2024.

sections.h2: What does Boston weather mean for a house?
sections.html:
Boston has hot, humid summers and cold, stormy winters, with occasional periods of heavy snow. Under one common classification it is humid subtropical, and under another it is humid continental.

  • July is the warmest month, with a mean temperature of 74.1 degrees F.
  • January is the coldest, with a mean of 29.9 degrees F.
  • The freezing window runs from about November 9 to April 5.
  • The most recent reading below zero was minus 10 degrees F on February 4, 2023, and sub-zero readings usually occur every three to five years.

Winters can bring wide swings, and in winter the immediate coast often sees rain where inland areas see snow.

sections.h2: How do Boston property tax and abatements work for a seller?
sections.html:
Massachusetts assessors value property as of January 1 before the fiscal year, and an owner who thinks the value is too high must first file an abatement application with the city's assessors. That application is due on or before the due date of the first actual tax bill. In towns that bill quarterly, that is generally February 1.

The Appellate Tax Board then hears appeals. It holds hearings at 100 Cambridge Street in Boston at Government Center, and often by video. Most single family hearings run one to two hours, and a case takes about four months to a year to reach a hearing.

We could not open the City of Boston's own assessing pages for this guide, so we are not quoting Boston's tax rate, residential exemption or billing dates. Ask the Boston Assessing Department for the current rate, whether your home qualifies for the residential exemption, and your abatement deadline. Your actual bill states the due dates.

sections.h2: What does a Boston closing involve?
sections.html:
Boston is in Suffolk County, so your deed is recorded at the Suffolk County Registry of Deeds. Massachusetts charges a deed excise tax when a deed is recorded. The neighboring Norfolk County registry lists $2.28 for each $500 of the price or fraction of it, and the same state statute applies in Suffolk County, so ask the Suffolk registry or your attorney for its fee schedule.

  • Smoke and carbon monoxide certificate. You need a certificate of compliance from the local fire department. Schedule the inspection as soon as you have a closing date, and expect to pay a fee.
  • Attorney involvement. A Massachusetts court has held that lender side closings need an attorney's substantive participation, so most sales involve a real estate attorney.
  • Home inspection. State regulation 760 CMR 74 stops sellers of certain residential properties from conditioning an offer on a waiver of the buyer's inspection.
  • Title systems. Most properties are recorded land, but some Massachusetts property is registered land with a Land Court certificate.

The Secretary of the Commonwealth also runs a registry consumer notification service that emails you when a new document is recorded against your property. That is worth signing up for if you are selling an inherited home or one with a title question.

sections.h2: What should a Boston seller with tenants know?
sections.html:
Many Boston houses have more than one unit. If yours does, ask the city's Inspectional Services Department whether the building must be registered or inspected as a rental, and ask your attorney how existing leases transfer to a buyer. We left city rental rules out of this page because we could not confirm them from an official Boston page.

A direct sale lets you skip showings while tenants stay in place. We buy Boston houses as they are, and you can compare our number with a listing price before you decide.

faqs.q: How many neighborhoods does Boston have?
faqs.a: The city's Office of Neighborhood Services designates 23 neighborhoods, including Back Bay, Dorchester, Jamaica Plain, South Boston and the North End.
Suffolk County. Deeds for Boston property are recorded at the Suffolk County Registry of Deeds.

faqs.q: Who are the biggest employers in Boston?
faqs.a: The 2023 top ten list is led by Brigham and Women's Hospital, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Massachusetts General Hospital and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Boston property tax assessment?
faqs.a: File an abatement application with the Boston assessors on or before the due date of your first actual tax bill. If it is denied or ignored, you have three months to appeal to the Appellate Tax Board.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke detector certificate to sell a Boston house?
faqs.a: Yes. Massachusetts requires a certificate of compliance from the local fire department showing your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms meet the rules for a sale of a one or two family home.
